48eae6652508275bf04c0e275388f1d97aea2bd9.summary: A 2014 LogRhythm blog post presents a proof of concept that shows how a fake Windows error alert with a login prompt can capture a user's plain-text password once an attacker has administrative rights on a host. The author notes that a similar macOS prompt can be run over SSH. The post treats the technique as simple and says adversaries have many avenues. Defensive advice: disable or restrict SSH and PowerShell Remoting on desktops, rely on log data, and use network segmentation and a filtering web proxy with SSL inspection. The report names no threat actor, sector, country, CVE or figure.

4846c7ed62c0ca85742c78bb1d2cef764341ca6e.summary: A news article says the cybercrime group FIN7 weaponized the Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) attachment technique within a day of it being published. Morphisec researchers compiled a timeline showing FIN7 adopts new techniques within a couple of days of detection and changes code to evade pattern-based detection. The group is described as a financial cybercrime group thought to be behind many online bank thefts, and was suspected of an SEC-themed spear-phishing attack. Cisco Talos saw a similar DDE attack. Fileless malware and social engineering are central to its tactics.
